newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Asian markets extend rebound from last week.
newsitem.headline: Asian markets extend rebound from last week.

text.p: HONG KONG - Asian stock markets on Tuesday extended their recovery from a correction last week as investors took heart in an overnight surge in New York stocks.

Asian investors, fuelling a second straight day of share-price gains, read the Dow's rise as a sign that U.S. markets had shrugged off last week's negative comments by Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan, brokers said.
Tokyo's Nikkei 225 index climbed 218.41 points, or 1.06 percent, to close at 20,822.12, while Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index surged 198.23 points to close at 13,342.46, a gain of 1.51 percent.
Markets in Australia, Malaysia, Singapore, the Philippines and Taiwan also rose.
"We are moving in line with the Dow," said Peter Lai, associate director at OCBC Securities in Hong Kong.

The Dow Jones industrial average had jumped 82 points on Monday to 6,463.94, its biggest point gain in more than a month, after finance officials downplayed Greenspan's comments about "irrational exuberance" in financial markets.

Stock markets around the world interpreted the remarks as a hint that the Fed was poised to raise interest rates to keep the U.S. market from overheating, provoking a sell-off worldwide on Friday that was partially recouped on Monday.
"For the Tokyo market, the plunge of over 650 points last week may have been a blessing in disguise, providing it with energy to bounce back," said a broker.

Australian shares closed firmer, though brokers said the market's gain was slightly disappointing given the Dow's 82-point surge on Monday. The All Ordinaries index ended 22 points higher at 2,361.8, a gain of 0.94 percent.
Secondary stocks led the Kuala Lumpur market's rise in late-morning dealings, with blue chips showing a mixed trend, traders said. At midday, the key Composite Index was up 9.88 points to 1,213.24.
Singapore's Straits Times Industrials Index rose 14.51 points to 2,211.64 on the Dow's strength, brokers said.
"But volume is low," one dealer said. "Most markets in Asia will remain cautious."
Seoul stocks closed up 10.66 points, or 1.54 percent, at a provisional 702.83.
Taiwan share prices also finished slightly higher, but brokers said worries over possible inflation and a lack of market-boosting news slowed buying interest.
The weighted index closed up 32.2 points or 0.47 percent at 6,841.03.
The Philippine equities market rebounded from a 1.57 percent drop on Monday, gaining back 38.22 points, or 1.24 percent, to close at 3,128.38 thanks to Wall Street, traders said.
Jakarta shares defied the regionwide optimism, slipping 6.84 points, or 1.08 percent, to 627.74 in late afternoon trade, dragged down by falls in the share price of heavyweight Telkom.
The Thai stock market was closed for a holiday.
